result.summary: I added `GithubImporter._import_inline_images(markdown, obj, repository_full_name, created_date)` in `taiga/importers/github/importer.py`. For each distinct GitHub inline image URL, it renders `![image]()` with `render_markdown` and reads the src of the first ``. It downloads that signed URL with `download`, rejects content that is not an image, and takes the file name from the Content-Disposition base name, or uses `github-attachment-` when there is none. It then creates the `Attachment` as specified, saves the file and returns `#`. If one image fails, its link stays, `logger.warning` is called, and the next image is processed. The user story and issue imports call it after the object is created and save the description only if it changed. Results: 7 new integration tests pass, `make check-fast` passes (233), and the full suite passes (1753 passed). I ran the full suite with pytest and a separate test database, because `make test` failed in `db-up`: port 5432 is used by another worktree's Postgres. Nothing was committed.

changes.summary: Module logger and imports for Attachment and ContentType. Helpers for URL replacement, reading the img src, header lookup and Content-Disposition file names. New methods `_import_inline_images`, `_import_inline_image` and `_import_description_inline_images`, called in both import loops.
7 tests: URL rewrite, URL imported once, attachment fields, fallback file name, failures keep the link and log a warning, and an end-to-end import as user stories and as issues.

acceptance.criterion: Imported user stories and issues point to local copies of their GitHub images, and a failed image keeps its link
The change is covered by tests
The existing test suite still passes
acceptance.evidence: Full suite: 1753 passed in 829 s. make check-fast: 233 passed.
